dependency_edges.handoff: The gradient sizes the momentum trade.
The distance from the mean sizes the reversion trade.
The gradient history triggers the override.
An extreme episode followed by a sale starts the no-buy window.
The two profitability readings are compared through the weight.
A sale is blocked during the holding period.

models.purpose: Issue a buy or sell signal from the price gradient and the moving average.
models.summary: The gradient is written two ways on one line, joined by or: a symbol form and a one-step discrete difference. The moving average is a weighted mean over the last n prices. A buy signal needs both the gradient and the price-minus-average gap to clear 1, and it stays active for exactly one step.

variables.definition: Price of the asset at time t.
The current day.
The number of days the metric looks back. The paper calls it the time interval observed.
The symbol form of the gradient, printed as the gradient of P.
The n-day gradient at time t, printed as approximately the price now minus the price n-1 days back.
The weight given to the price i days back.
The weighted average of the last n prices.
The braced quantity that is either the gradient or the gap between price and average.

governing_equations.source_expression: G = grad P or G_t(n) approx P_t - P_(t-n+1)
governing_equations.purpose: Give the gradient in symbol form and in discrete form on one line.
The weighted moving average over the window.
The two cases the signal can take, each glossed in parentheses.

equation_status.reason: Three display formulas, all read off the page.

objectives: Capitalize on price increases by combining the gradient and the moving average.
constraints: A buy signal requires both G_t(n) > 1 and P_t - A_t(n) > 1.

parameter_estimation.method: The threshold of 1 is stated with no derivation.

steps: Compute the gradient over the window.
Compute the weighted moving average.
Issue a buy signal if both exceed 1, and keep it active until t + 1.
Otherwise issue a sell signal.
algorithm.convergence_criteria: No iteration; the signal is a direct comparison.

assumptions: The technique is called common and is not cited.

identifiability_feasibility.analysis: The threshold 1 is never justified, so the signal level is not identifiable from the text.

models.computational_cost: Two sums and two comparisons per asset per day.
strengths: The signal names its own lifespan: active until the next time period.
limitations: The brace says or while the following sentence says both cases must be true.
missing_details: No value is given for the weights w_i.

models.purpose: Add a buy signal for prices that fall below the moving average.
models.summary: Opened by conceding that momentum only sees breakouts above the average. The formula is an inequality of two integrals of the price density, and the paper translates it twice: once as an operational rule and once qualitatively.

variables.definition: The mean the price is assumed to revert to.
The wider integration half-width. Printed i.
The narrower integration half-width. Printed j.
The price distribution integrated over each band. Printed P(x).
The qualitative conclusion: a price far below the average is a buy.

governing_equations.source_expression: integral_{mu-i}^{mu+i} P(x) dx > integral_{mu-j}^{mu+j} P(x) dx for i > j > 0
governing_equations.purpose: State that the wider band carries more probability mass than the narrower one.

equation_status.reason: One display inequality, read off the page.

objectives: Catch downward moves that momentum trading ignores.
constraints: The inequality is only asserted for i > j > 0.

parameter_estimation.method: No parameter is fitted; the relation is stipulated.

steps: Compare the price with the moving average.
Treat a large deviation below the average as a buy.
algorithm.convergence_criteria: No convergence claim; the rule is qualitative.

assumptions: The price reverts toward the moving average, as assumed in section 1.3.3.

identifiability_feasibility.analysis: P(x) is never defined or estimated, so the integral cannot be computed from the given data.

models.computational_cost: Not computed numerically; used as a qualitative rule.
strengths: The formula is translated into prose twice, at two levels of formality.
missing_details: No threshold converts the inequality into a trade size.

models.purpose: Turn each buy signal into an amount.
models.summary: Two stipulations, each introduced with we say that. Momentum profitability grows with the gradient. Reversion profitability grows with the square of the distance from the mean. Neither is written as a formula.

variables.definition: Said to be proportional to the price gradient.
Said to be proportional to the square of the distance from the mean.
The gradient from section 3.1, reused as the momentum metric.
How far the price sits from the moving average.

equation_status.reason: Both rules are spoken proportionalities. No equation is printed.

objectives: Size the trade by how strong the signal is.
constraints: The proportionality constants are never stated.

steps: For a momentum trade, scale the amount with the gradient.
For a reversion trade, scale the amount with the square of the distance from the mean.
Buy only if the profitability clears an unnamed threshold, as the flow chart states.

assumptions: The price reverts to the mean, so a large drop is read as a crash and bought in size.

identifiability_feasibility.analysis: Without the constants, the trade size is not determined by the text.

strengths: The crash rule is stated as a recognition rather than a threshold.
limitations: The threshold in the flow chart is unnamed.
missing_details: No proportionality constant for either rule.
The buy threshold has no value.

models.purpose: Sell when the price clears the average cost paid, after fees and a margin.
models.summary: Characterized up front as simple and conservative. The sell indicator subtracts the fee-adjusted average cost and a margin from the fee-adjusted price. The whole formula is then restated in prose with the gold fee substituted, and the rule ends in six words.

variables.definition: Positive when the model sells.
The transaction fee rate for the asset.
The current price of the asset.
The fee rate paid on the i-th earlier purchase. Printed f with subscript a_i.
The cost paid for the asset on the i-th purchase.
The number of purchases averaged over. Printed n.
The margin the profit must clear.

governing_equations.purpose: Compare the fee-adjusted price with the average fee-adjusted cost plus a margin.

equation_status.reason: One display formula, read off the page and restated in the prose.

objectives: Sell only when the gain exceeds the average cost by a margin.
constraints: The model sells only if S > 0.

parameter_estimation.method: The margin L is named but never valued.

steps: Compute the fee-adjusted sale proceeds.
Subtract the average fee-adjusted cost of the lots held.
Subtract the margin.
Sell if the result is positive.

assumptions: The price oscillates, so a rise is followed by a fall.

identifiability_feasibility.analysis: The fee rates are given elsewhere as 1 and 2 percent, but L is free.

models.computational_cost: One average and one comparison per asset per day.
strengths: The formula is repeated in prose with a gloss after each term.
missing_details: L is never assigned a number.

models.purpose: Block selling during a rapid price rise.
models.summary: The trigger is stated in prose as a gradient over five times the historical average, then printed with a free scaling factor C, and the two are not reconciled. While active, selling is forbidden until the price falls to a percentage of its peak or a fixed amount below it.

variables.definition: Positive when the extreme-market rule takes over.
The current gradient from section 3.1.
Printed C. The prose says five times; the formula leaves it free.
The number of past gradients averaged.
The amount below the interval maximum that ends the override. Printed as a capital delta P.

governing_equations.purpose: Compare the current gradient with a scaled average of past gradients.

equation_status.reason: One display formula, read off the page.

objectives: Avoid selling before a rapid rise has finished.
constraints: No selling while E is positive, until the price regresses.

parameter_estimation.method: C is called a scaling factor and the prose separately says five.

steps: Compare the current gradient with the scaled historical average.
If positive, hand control to the extreme-market rule and skip the rest of the day.
Resume selling only after the price falls to a percentage of its peak or delta P below it.

assumptions: A rapid rise is followed by a regression rather than a further surge.

identifiability_feasibility.analysis: The prose factor of five and the symbol C disagree, and neither exit threshold is numbered.

models.computational_cost: One running average per asset per day.
strengths: The rule names the failure it prevents: a premature sell.
limitations: The scaling factor is stated two ways.
missing_details: The percentage of the maximum is never given.

models.purpose: Stop the model trading on small moves and on the way down from a peak.
models.summary: Two prose rules with no formula. After an extreme episode and a sale, buying is barred for a number of days. After any purchase, selling is barred for z days. The reason is named in one word: fees.

variables.definition: Days after a purchase during which the model may not sell.
Days after an extreme episode and a sale during which the model may not buy. The paper says a number of days.
Whether the model is allowed to buy or sell today.

equation_status.reason: Both rules are prohibitions written in prose. No equation is printed.

objectives: Keep fees from dominating the profit by suppressing small trades.
constraints: No buying during the no-buy window.
No selling during the z days after a purchase.

parameter_estimation.method: z is a symbol with no value and the no-buy window has no symbol.

steps: Check the no-buy flag and the extreme-market flag first.
If neither blocks the day, evaluate the sell indicators.
Compare the buy indicators and store the decision.
Execute sells before buys.
algorithm.convergence_criteria: No iteration; the day is a fixed sequence.

assumptions: Small corrections during a large move should not trigger a sale.
Another surge immediately after a peak is unlikely.

identifiability_feasibility.analysis: Neither duration is determined by the text.

strengths: The reason is labeled explicitly and the tempting alternative is conceded before it is overturned.
limitations: The no-buy duration is deliberately vague.
missing_details: The no-buy window has no number.

models.purpose: Shrink the influence of small late signals so the two assets can be compared.
models.summary: Introduced by resemblance: a weight factor that goes like one over C t squared. It falls as time grows, which the paper calls drowning out small changes, and it makes the bitcoin signal count for more than the gold signal.

variables.definition: The factor applied when the two assets' signals are compared.
Printed C. A free scalar.
Time in days. Printed t.

governing_equations.purpose: Down-weight signals as the record grows.

equation_status.reason: One display formula, read off the page.

objectives: Compare gold and bitcoin on the same scale despite their different magnitudes.
constraints: The weight is always positive and shrinks with time.

parameter_estimation.method: C is called a scalar constant and never valued.

steps: Compute the weight from the day index.
Apply it when the profitability of the two assets is compared.

assumptions: The two assets differ in the magnitude of their moves, as figure 2 shows.

identifiability_feasibility.analysis: The shape is fixed but the scale constant is free.

strengths: The effect is stated as a limit in words before it is used.
limitations: The same letter C was a scaling factor two subsections earlier.
missing_details: The paper does not say which asset's signal the weight multiplies.
